project.name: LunaNexa
project.tagline: Operate a private GPU fleet as a governed model provider.
project.description: A newcomer-friendly coursebook for learning, using, deploying, and troubleshooting LunaNexa.

pages.title: What is LunaNexa?
pages.summary: LunaNexa is the model-as-a-service and GPU-cluster control plane between authorized model consumers and a private hardware fleet. It governs models, nodes, placement, inference, access, evidence, and recovery without turning managed nodes into application servers.
pages.audience: New platform operators, infrastructure engineers, and model-service clients

blocks.text: The one-sentence mental model

Applications ask for a generic model capability. LunaNexa authenticates and admits that request, selects a ready deployment on an eligible node, invokes an approved serving adapter, and returns normalized output plus auditable usage and timing evidence.

steps.title: Consumer intent
steps.text: An authorized client sends a provider-neutral workload envelope.

steps.title: Control plane
steps.text: Policy, quota, lease, model, and capacity checks decide whether work may run.

steps.title: Node runtime
steps.text: A selected DGX runs only an approved, digest-pinned model server.

steps.title: Bounded result
steps.text: The client receives normalized output, usage, timing, status, and a receipt.

blocks.title: Tomorrow's deployment is still an acceptance run
blocks.text: The repository has a deployable baseline and extensive simulation evidence. It has not manufactured the missing physical-DGX, production identity, model-license, runtime-image, performance, and named-human acceptance evidence.

blocks.question: What is the most important architectural boundary?
blocks.answer: Application and product decisions stop above LunaNexa. Managed GPU nodes receive only LunaNexa infrastructure, approved runtime containers, signed model artifacts, and bounded telemetry.

pages.title: What works now—and what still needs proof?
pages.summary: The software baseline is broad and tested, but production readiness remains conditional on the real four-node cluster and external trust infrastructure. Read this page before interpreting any green local test as a production guarantee.

blocks.text: Implemented repository baseline

items: Typed workload, node, assignment, registry, workspace, deployment, telemetry, audit, and streaming contracts.
Native controller, node agent, scheduler, client/CLI, durable state, PostgreSQL management adapter, and recovery tooling.
Rabbita management console, enterprise portal, developer workbench, and a scoped VS Code extension.
Signed assignments, digest and Cosign checks, strict per-node runtime routing, bounded admission, cancellation, and receipt-bearing failures.
Four-node functional simulation, restart drills, isolation scans, secret scans, response-leak checks, and browser tests.

blocks.text: External acceptance gates

rows: Enroll all physical nodes and exercise real heartbeats, scheduling, drain, restart, and failover.
Select a licensed model and signed ARM64 runtime image; qualify vLLM or SGLang on the actual DGX.
Configure and verify CA/mTLS termination, subject mapping, scoped credentials, rotation, and network isolation.
Deploy HA or managed PostgreSQL, encrypted backups, storage classes, and tested restoration.
Measure cold start, long stream, concurrency, saturation, memory, thermal, drain, and failure on hardware.
Obtain named operations, security, and model-license approvals after inspecting live evidence.

blocks.title: No guarantee by substitution
blocks.text: A successful Colima/kind run, fake four-node simulator, or digest-valid YAML document does not prove NVIDIA device discovery, ARM64 image compatibility, production networking, thermal stability, or real service objectives.

blocks.question: When may EvidenceBundle.release_ready() become true?
blocks.answer: Only when benchmark evidence, report references, scenario and isolation success, and a named acceptor are all present.

pages.title: Know the trust and product boundaries
pages.summary: LunaNexa is deliberately narrow: it manages model capacity and hardware authority. It does not become an application platform, agent runtime, identity provider, secret manager, container registry, object store, or metrics database.
pages.audience: Architects, security reviewers, and integration developers

blocks.text: The managed-node rule

blocks.title: Allowed on a managed DGX
blocks.text: The LunaNexa node agent, an approved model-runtime container, the exact signed model artifacts named by an assignment, host-owned trust material, and bounded infrastructure telemetry.

blocks.title: Forbidden on a managed DGX
blocks.text: MoonSuite applications, repository checkouts, domain schemas, editor agents, application credentials, arbitrary controller-supplied shell commands, and product-specific workflows.
Structural isolation is not payload absence

A model must receive the user content it processes. LunaNexa therefore treats structural isolation as absolute while applying minimization, transport encryption, explicit data classification, no logging by default, and explicit retention policy to inference payloads.
Workspace lease versus exclusive-node lease

rows: Time-bounded control-plane admission and generic model capability limits
DGX login, shell, repository checkout, or node filesystem access
One named subject, one named DGX, time-bounded host access under a separate guarded lifecycle
Concurrent managed inference placement or an application-level workflow

blocks.question: May the browser workbench install an editor agent on a managed node?
blocks.answer: No. It keeps editing state in the browser/workspace domain and invokes LunaNexa through the provider-neutral workload contract.

blocks.title: Fixed fleet by design
blocks.text: The initial production profile has four schedulable DGX Spark nodes, no autoscaling, and no batch subsystem. Capacity and placement changes are explicit operator actions.

pages.title: Understand the architecture
pages.summary: The architecture separates consumer intent, management authority, node reconciliation, and inference traffic. The management node owns durable control state; each DGX is an independently schedulable execution node.

steps.title: Consumers
steps.text: MoonGate or another authorized client sends the generic LunaNexa contract.

steps.title: Management domain
steps.text: API, scheduler, controller, registry, stores, PostgreSQL, console, enterprise portal, and workbench govern intent.

steps.title: Node domain
steps.text: One protected node agent per DGX reconciles signed assignments and supervises approved OCI runtimes.

steps.title: Inference result
steps.text: The selected ready adapter produces bounded output and evidence through the control plane.

blocks.text: Initial four-node topology

Treat the four Sparks as four independent nodes. Single-node serving is the first acceptance target. Multi-node sharding is disabled until the real network, runtime, model, and topology pass a named benchmark.

blocks.title: The management node is not a compute node
blocks.text: It joins Kubernetes and receives the management placement label, but it must not enroll into the LunaNexa compute-node inventory.

pages.title: Follow state ownership and durability
pages.summary: Not all state lives in PostgreSQL. Enterprise and workspace authority use transactional PostgreSQL projections; controller, registry, scheduler, enrollment, telemetry, deployment, and exclusive-lease stores still use signed file/PVC adapters and epoch fencing.
pages.audience: Operator planning storage, backup, or recovery

Back up PostgreSQL with encryption and test point-in-time restore.

PostgreSQL in production; file adapter for development
Preserve admission ownership and rolling counters across restart.

steps.title: Persist intent
steps.text: Write canonical state and projections atomically before publishing effects.

steps.title: Advance epoch
steps.text: A restarted controller acquires a strictly newer fencing epoch.

steps.title: Reconcile only
steps.text: Inspect missing assignments, expired leases, orphans, and unreachable nodes without accepting writes.

steps.title: Resume authority
steps.text: Accept mutations only after the recovery plan and audit continuity are reviewed.

blocks.title: Reference PostgreSQL is not HA
blocks.text: deploy/postgres.yaml is a single-instance reference. Production should use an approved managed service or operator with replication, failover, TLS verification, encrypted storage, WAL archiving, and point-in-time recovery.

pages.title: Trace an inference request
pages.summary: A workload crosses validation, identity, lease, policy, scheduler, runtime, and evidence boundaries. Each stage can reject safely before model execution, and terminal failures use the same canonical response shape.
pages.audience: API client developer and on-call operator

steps.title: Validate envelope
steps.text: Contract version, opaque ids, model selector, data policy, deadline, ceilings, and payload shape are checked.

steps.title: Resolve authority
steps.text: Credential scope and, when enabled, verified subject, active grant, active workspace lease, rate, and held concurrency are enforced.

steps.title: Admit and place
steps.text: Quota and capacity are reserved; hard filters remove ineligible nodes; deterministic scoring selects a ready deployment.

steps.title: Invoke adapter
steps.text: Strict node-to-HTTPS mapping or a trusted node-aware gateway reaches the selected digest-matched runtime.

steps.title: Normalize evidence
steps.text: Output, usage, queue time, accelerator time, runtime/model identity, status, retryability, and receipt are returned and audited.

blocks.text: Idempotency and ownership

Clients use a unique opaque workload ID and idempotency key per logical operation. While a workload is queued or running, a duplicate is rejected as WorkloadAlreadyActive. With workspace enforcement, durable admission state binds status and cancellation to the original authenticated subject and tenant.
Streaming and failure semantics

items: Streaming is bounded and rejects truncated completion rather than pretending success.
Alternate-node failover is allowed only before the first output is delivered.
Caller cancellation becomes CancelledByCaller.
Queue or runtime deadline expiry becomes non-retryable DeadlineExceeded.
Adapter loss becomes RuntimeUnavailable with retryability derived from the failure class.

blocks.title: Declared size is not trusted
blocks.text: Workspace admission measures UTF-8 bytes of canonical payload JSON and requires the actual size to fit both the request ceiling and lease limit.

blocks.question: Why can LunaNexa retry only before the first streamed output?
blocks.answer: Once output reaches the caller, retrying on another node could duplicate or contradict visible results. Pre-output retry preserves one logical response boundary.

pages.title: Trace a model-service deployment
pages.summary: One-click deployment is compact at the API but strict underneath: a signed catalog template expands into preflight, durable operation state, selected-node assignments, verified artifact materialization, runtime readiness, promotion, and audit evidence.

steps.title: Signed template
steps.text: Pins model artifact, runtime image, policies, resources, health profile, secrets, and rollout rules.

steps.title: Deterministic plan
steps.text: Validates approvals, license, evaluation, signatures, secret references, data class, capacity, and node readiness.

steps.title: Durable operation
steps.text: Persists idempotent intent and selected nodes before publishing assignments.

steps.title: Node materialization
steps.text: Only selected nodes pull the assignment-bound object, verify size, digest, and signature, and publish a local read-only cache entry.

steps.title: Runtime readiness
steps.text: A digest-pinned OCI runtime starts with the verified local artifact and reports health through the node agent.

steps.title: Promote or recover
steps.text: Operator inspects evidence, promotes, rolls back, or deletes through audited operations.

blocks.text: Blocked is a durable result

When a prerequisite is missing, LunaNexa does not launch partially. The deployment operation remains durable in Blocked with typed preflight findings. Reusing the same idempotency key returns the same operation rather than creating duplicate assignments.

rows: Deploying unapproved or unlicensed model bytes
Full model digest and detached signature
Full runtime image digest and approval
Running a mutable or unreviewed image
Scheduling a model on an unsupported architecture
Starting a runtime whose deployment-owned dependency is absent
Claiming a static inventory label is a serving runtime

blocks.title: No controller SSH or copy channel
blocks.text: The management plane publishes signed assignments. The selected node pulls the exact object through an assignment-scoped gateway grant; the controller does not open an arbitrary shell or file-copy path.

pages.title: Trace node enrollment and reconciliation
pages.summary: Kubernetes registration and LunaNexa enrollment are separate. The management node joins and receives a management label; each DGX joins as a worker, receives the GPU label, then enrolls with one-use bootstrap material and a unique persistent node credential.

rows: Enroll once with bootstrap token; retain unique node credential

steps.title: Prepare host
steps.text: Verify stable node name, architecture, GPU inventory, runtime engine, trust files, and protected state paths.

steps.title: Issue bootstrap
steps.text: Create a short-lived one-use enrollment token bound to that node's private enrollment request.

steps.title: Enroll
steps.text: The controller stores only a digest of the persistent node credential and issues bounded certificate evidence.

steps.title: Heartbeat
steps.text: The node signs replay-fenced inventory, runtime readiness, capacity, telemetry, and lease observations.

steps.title: Reconcile
steps.text: The node accepts only current signed assignments whose generation, epoch, lease, artifact, and runtime identities match.

blocks.label: Verify Kubernetes identity before enrollment
blocks.code:
kubectl get node MANAGEMENT_NODE -L lunanexa.io/role
kubectl get node dgx-spark-01 -L lunanexa.io/role
kubectl describe node dgx-spark-01 | sed -n '/Capacity:/,/Allocatable:/p'

blocks.title: Identity must agree everywhere
blocks.text: The Kubernetes node name, LUNANEXA_NODE_ID, and inventory.json node_id must name the same stable DGX. Do not proceed on an alias or copied credential.

pages.title: Trace user, workspace, and exclusive access
pages.summary: Human access is explicit and layered: external identity maps to an opaque subject, an operator activates the user and grant, a bounded lease authorizes model admission, and a separate exclusive-node contract governs any real DGX login.

steps.title: Authenticate externally
steps.text: Trusted ingress validates the human and derives or injects an opaque LunaNexa subject.

steps.title: Register user
steps.text: The operator creates or invites a workspace user, then activates the lifecycle record.

steps.title: Grant access
steps.text: A tenant-scoped Developer or Admin grant defines role and time window.

steps.title: Activate lease
steps.text: A capability lease limits requests, concurrency, input/output, and expiry.

steps.title: Invoke
steps.text: Workbench or client presents inference authority; the server resolves subject ownership and admits only a matching active grant and lease.

blocks.text: Production identity transport

With ingress-nginx client certificates, only ssl-client-verify: SUCCESS is accepted and the distinguished name is reduced to an opaque SHA-256 subject reference. X-LunaNexa-Subject is accepted only from an actual loopback TCP peer; remote callers cannot self-assert it.
Exclusive-node lifecycle

steps.title: Reserve
steps.text: One user and one eligible DGX are bound; managed placement is fenced immediately.

steps.title: Provision
steps.text: A fixed root-owned helper resolves a credential reference and applies allowlisted host operations.

steps.title: Expire or end
steps.text: The protected node watchdog enforces generation and time even while disconnected.

steps.title: Revoke and sanitize
steps.text: Access removal and cleanup must produce current receipts.

steps.title: Return or quarantine
steps.text: Only proven sanitization returns the node to managed service; failure quarantines it.

blocks.title: Identity directory is not an IdP
blocks.text: LunaNexa stores opaque subject references and evidence, not upstream passwords, identity documents, browser credentials, or client private keys.

pages.title: Run the local functional path
pages.summary: Use the repository gate and dedicated simulations to validate behavior on a development machine. These commands prove software contracts and local orchestration—not DGX performance or production security.

items.title: Run four-node behavior directly

items.title: Run Kubernetes placement smoke

blocks.title: Expected local result
blocks.text: The command must show exactly one Ready management node and four Ready gpu-labelled workers. It was exercised on an Apple-silicon Mac with Colima; it remains a placement simulation with no NVIDIA device or production-identity claim.

blocks.title: Read the evidence, not only the exit code
blocks.text: The simulator deliberately records hardware_performance_validated: false. Do not remove or reinterpret that boundary.

pages.title: Use the management console
pages.summary: The Rabbita console is the operator surface for cluster posture, nodes, models, deployments, users, grants, leases, policies, requests, benchmarks, and audit evidence. It sends the same typed API mutations used by automation.

items.title: Connect through trusted ingress
items.text: Use operator authority and verified transport identity; do not expose the controller HTTP listener directly.

items.title: Read Overview first
items.text: Confirm cluster posture, capacity, queues, alerts, and recent changes before taking an action.

items.title: Inspect evidence behind state
items.text: A green label is not enough—open the assignment, model, deployment, request, or audit detail and confirm the current receipt and source state.

items.title: Use confirmation boundaries
items.text: Cordon, drain, rollback, revoke, suspend, and early lease termination show scope and require explicit confirmation.

items.title: Verify convergence

pages.title: Use the developer workbench and editor clients
pages.summary: The workbench is a browser-local editing and model-invocation surface. It displays identity, grant, lease, capability, expiry, and receipt state while keeping repository content and editor agents outside managed DGX nodes.
pages.audience: Developer with an active workspace lease

items.title: Connect identity
items.text: The browser reads /v1/workspace/self through trusted ingress and displays the mapped subject's current authorization.

items.title: Confirm active capability
items.text: A valid user, tenant grant, active time window, and TextGenerate lease must agree before Send is enabled.

items.title: Edit locally
items.text: Project drafts remain browser-local; the workbench is not a remote DGX filesystem or shell.

items.title: Invoke explicitly
items.text: The client sends a canonical ephemeral request with bounded input/output and a unique workload/idempotency identity.

items.title: Inspect result evidence
items.text: Read normalized output, status, usage, timing, and receipt; server rejection remains authoritative if a lease expires mid-session.

blocks.text: External editors

rows: Working scoped client over explicitly selected text
Token in SecretStorage, bound to approved origin and machine-scoped settings
Vendor credentials and agent runtime stay with the external client
Bearer credential stays in browser memory for the active session

blocks.title: Session fields are not inference enforcement yet
blocks.text: max_active_sessions and max_session_duration_ms are validated policy for a future server-side WorkspaceSession service. Current inference enforcement uses per-capability request concurrency and rate limits.

pages.title: Integrate a provider-neutral client
pages.summary: Clients use LunaNexa's canonical workload contract rather than sending application identity or provider-specific assumptions to the cluster. Compatibility APIs are adapters, not the source of truth.

blocks.text: Client responsibilities

items: Translate application authority and data policy into the generic WorkloadEnvelope outside LunaNexa.
Use opaque tenant, workload, correlation, and idempotency values that reveal no product identity.
Select a published model alias or capability, never a repository path or internal node address.
Honor typed retryability, deadlines, cancellation, and receipt-bearing terminal results.
Keep provider fallback and application policy in the consumer repository.

blocks.title: Never put these in the workload
blocks.text: Application credentials, repository paths, product names, editor state, internal runtime URLs, node credentials, or secret-provider values.

pages.title: Deploy the management node and first DGX safely
pages.summary: Tomorrow's safe order is management host, Kubernetes placement, management plane, health and ingress, then one DGX at a time. Do not enroll the management node and do not start with all four workers simultaneously.

steps.title: Render management plane

steps.title: Migrate and start
steps.text: Apply prerequisites, PostgreSQL, controller, console, enterprise/workbench, network policy, and ingress; run database migration with owner authority.

steps.title: Verify boundary

steps.title: Enroll DGX 1
steps.text: Join worker, label GPU role, verify NVIDIA/runtime/trust material, issue one-use bootstrap, enroll, remove bootstrap material, and observe heartbeat.

steps.title: Repeat deliberately

blocks.title: Private overlay is mandatory
blocks.text: Base manifests contain placeholders and do not fully enforce management versus GPU placement. Do not apply them unchanged to a real cluster.

blocks.title: Use the installer UI within its boundary
blocks.text: The assisted UI begins with pinned-host SSH verification after hosts have already joined Kubernetes. It does not accept arbitrary shell commands, SSH keys, kubeadm join tokens, or browser-stored secrets.

pages.title: Qualify vLLM or SGLang on DGX Spark
pages.summary: The repository now has secret-free single-node qualification templates for vLLM and SGLang. They test a real ARM64 DGX and verified local model directory but are not a second production deployment path.

blocks.text: Prerequisites

items: Recorded DGX OS, kernel, ARM64 architecture, NVIDIA driver, CUDA, and container-runtime versions.
NVIDIA Kubernetes device plugin exposes nvidia.com/gpu and RuntimeClass/nvidia exists or the reviewed overlay uses the cluster default.
The selected node is labelled lunanexa.io/role=gpu and pinned by exact kubernetes.io/hostname.
A verified Hugging Face-format directory exists only on that DGX under /var/lib/lunanexa/qualification-models/sha256/<digest>/model.
The runtime image is ARM64, signed, scanned, and pinned by a complete SHA-256 digest.

rows: 1 GPU, TP=1, bfloat16, 0.80 GPU memory, 8192 context
OpenAI-compatible chat; Responses compatibility must be proven or adapted
1 GPU, TP=1, bfloat16, 0.80 static memory, 8192 context

blocks.label: Qualification sequence
blocks.code:
kubectl apply -f deploy/dgx-spark/runtime-qualification-prerequisites.yaml
kubectl apply -f RENDERED_VLLM.yaml
kubectl -n lunanexa-runtime-qualification rollout status deployment/vllm-dgx-spark --timeout=30m
kubectl -n lunanexa-runtime-qualification logs deployment/vllm-dgx-spark --tail=200

blocks.title: Current packaging gap
blocks.text: The LunaNexa materializer currently publishes one verified artifact file, while vLLM/SGLang normally consume a multi-file Hugging Face directory. Production promotion needs a reviewed assignment-bound packaging/extraction adapter that reverifies output before mounting it.
Evidence to retain

items: Exact runtime image, model tree/archive, and detached-signature digests.
Cold and warm start, time to first token, p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens per second, and memory pressure.
Malformed input, invalid model, cancellation, concurrency saturation, OOM rejection, process restart, and node drain.
A successful LunaNexa route and normalized streaming receipt through the approved HTTPS boundary.

pages.title: Run alerts, offline orders, machine access, and guide diagnostics
pages.summary: This newcomer-first runbook connects the operator console and customer portal: respond to durable alerts, correlate bounded operational evidence, reconcile offline commercial documents, follow exclusive-machine access through expiry, and use the role-safe guide diagnostics page.
pages.audience: New on-call operators, customer administrators, finance coordinators, and exclusive-machine users

blocks.text: Start with the right surface

rows: Alert center with severity, acknowledgement, assignment, silence window, resolution, source receipt, and delivery status
Tenant inbox with read/unread state and agreement, payment, document, lease, access, expiry, or termination updates
Bounded event stream, low-cardinality metrics, immutable audit receipts, and typed alert codes
Only the status and correlation receipt needed for the customer's own request
Quote, approval, artifact generation, exact-digest review, correction, and fulfillment controls
Order timeline, print packet readiness, upload-grant request, evidence status, and correction request
Lease state, forced-revocation policy, node reachability, sanitization, and quarantine
Own machine display name, username, access-handoff status/reference, coarse reachability, expiry, termination action, and sanitization status
Authenticated aggregate health, active alert codes, state counts, recovery backlog, skill names/versions, and runbook links
Public coursebook and read-only Ask guide, without live cluster state

blocks.title: One event, two audiences
blocks.text: A durable source event can appear as an actionable operator alert and as a tenant-scoped customer notification. Reading or dismissing a message does not erase the source receipt, and a delivery retry does not create another business event.
Recipe 1: triage an alert and confirm the customer message

items: Operator: open Alert center, sort Critical and High first, open one alert, and copy its correlation or source receipt before changing anything.
Operator: inspect the current evidence, then acknowledge ownership. Assign it to a named responder; use a bounded silence only when a maintenance window explains the signal.
Operator: resolve only after the typed condition has recovered. Resolution closes the alert lifecycle but preserves its evidence.
Customer: open Notifications in the enterprise portal, confirm the message belongs to the expected order or lease, follow its safe action, and mark it read.
If email, SMS, or webhook delivery fails, continue with the in-app record and investigate the operator DeliveryDeadLetter alert.

blocks.label: Operator read-only triage (credentials come from the secret provider)
blocks.code:
set -eu
: "${LUNANEXA_ENDPOINT:?set the approved LunaNexa API origin}"
: "${LUNANEXA_OPERATOR_TOKEN:?load operator authority without printing it}"
: "${LUNANEXA_MONITORING_TOKEN:?load monitoring authority without printing it}"

curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $LUNANEXA_OPERATOR_TOKEN" \
  "$LUNANEXA_ENDPOINT/v1/notifications/operator"

curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $LUNANEXA_MONITORING_TOKEN" \
  "$LUNANEXA_ENDPOINT/v1/observability/events"

curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $LUNANEXA_MONITORING_TOKEN" \
  "$LUNANEXA_ENDPOINT/metrics"

blocks.text: Recipe 2: correlate events, metrics, alerts, and audit

steps.title: Operational event
steps.text: The component emits bounded JSON with a stable event code, outcome, component, time, and correlation receipt.

steps.title: Metric update
steps.text: A counter, gauge, or latency series changes using low-cardinality labels; tenant, user, lease, and request identifiers never become metric labels.

steps.title: Typed rule
steps.text: A state or metric rule detects the condition. Rules do not parse human log prose.

steps.title: Durable alert
steps.text: The notification authority deduplicates the condition and opens or updates the operator record.

steps.title: Audit correlation
steps.text: For a consequential mutation, the immutable audit receipt explains actor class, prior state, next state, decision, and result.

blocks.title: Logs explain; they do not grant authority
blocks.text: Use the correlation receipt to join the alert, operational event, adapter call, and audit record. Never paste raw logs, tokens, document bytes, prompts, model output, SSH material, or callback bodies into a ticket or the guide.
Recipe 3: complete the hybrid offline workflow

steps.title: Configure online
steps.text: The customer selects the service, SLA, project, and requested expiry; the server derives tenant and purchaser identity.

steps.title: Prepare packet
steps.text: The operator applies the immutable quote and approved policy, obtains internal approval, and releases only renderer-verified print artifacts.

steps.title: Execute offline
steps.text: The customer prints the PDF and follows the existing physical seal, treasury collection, and invoice process.

steps.title: Upload evidence
steps.text: The customer requests a short-lived upload grant. The object store and scanner report the verified digest and safety result; the browser does not choose the object reference.

steps.title: Reconcile
steps.text: A reviewer who did not submit the evidence accepts or rejects the exact digest. Rejection keeps history and requests a replacement revision.

steps.title: Fulfill
steps.text: The operator creates the opaque entitlement only after every policy-required agreement, payment, invoice, identity, and approval item is accepted.

blocks.label: Customer and operator read-only order checks
blocks.code:
set -eu
: "${LUNANEXA_ENDPOINT:?set the approved LunaNexa API origin}"
: "${LUNANEXA_INFERENCE_TOKEN:?load customer API authority without printing it}"
: "${LUNANEXA_OPERATOR_TOKEN:?load operator authority without printing it}"
: "${LUNANEXA_CLIENT_CERT_PATH:?set the verified client certificate path}"
: "${LUNANEXA_CLIENT_KEY_PATH:?set the protected client key path}"

curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error \
  --cert "$LUNANEXA_CLIENT_CERT_PATH" --key "$LUNANEXA_CLIENT_KEY_PATH" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $LUNANEXA_INFERENCE_TOKEN" \
  "$LUNANEXA_ENDPOINT/v1/offline-commerce/self/orders"

curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $LUNANEXA_OPERATOR_TOKEN" \
  "$LUNANEXA_ENDPOINT/v1/offline-commerce/operator/snapshot"

blocks.title: A generated file is not a legal or financial outcome
blocks.text: The PDF is the print copy and the DOCX is an editable source. An upload is not an e-signature, a receipt is not bank settlement, and generated metadata is not a tax invoice. Keep the order paused until the organization's authorized legal and finance reviewers accept the required evidence.
Recipe 4: use and end an exclusive-machine lease safely

items: Customer: open Machine access and verify lease state, machine display name, username, coarse reachability, handoff state, start time, and expiry before connecting. The portal intentionally does not reveal the physical node ID or a raw credential.

Customer: follow the opaque handoff reference to the approved credential broker or SSH certificate redirect. That separate trusted surface supplies the authorized host alias, port, certificate, and host-key fingerprint; compare the fingerprint before the first login.
Customer: before manual termination, save work and stop personal processes. Review the current lease generation, type the exact confirmation shown by the portal, and submit once.
Operator: watch Draining, RevokingAccess, and Sanitizing. Do not restore managed scheduling merely because the account disappeared.
Operator: return the node to managed service only after the current sanitization receipt is verified; quarantine and alert on any cleanup failure.

blocks.label: Customer read-only access and notification checks
blocks.code:
set -eu
: "${LUNANEXA_ENDPOINT:?set the approved LunaNexa API origin}"
: "${LUNANEXA_INFERENCE_TOKEN:?load customer API authority without printing it}"
: "${LUNANEXA_CLIENT_CERT_PATH:?set the verified client certificate path}"
: "${LUNANEXA_CLIENT_KEY_PATH:?set the protected client key path}"

for path in /v1/machine-access/self /v1/notifications/self; do
  curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error \
    --cert "$LUNANEXA_CLIENT_CERT_PATH" --key "$LUNANEXA_CLIENT_KEY_PATH" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $LUNANEXA_INFERENCE_TOKEN" \
    "$LUNANEXA_ENDPOINT$path"
done

blocks.title: Exclusive does not mean root
blocks.text: The initial offering is an exclusive non-root account with a documented filesystem boundary and rootless containers. It does not grant sudo, management-node access, LunaNexa daemon credentials, another tenant's data, or permission to disable the node-local expiry guard.
Recipe 5: use the guide without crossing roles

rows: Live cluster state, private evidence, raw logs, credentials, or operator actions
Aggregate component health, active alert codes/counts, node and lease state counts, recovery backlog, knowledge revision, enabled skill names/versions, missing evidence, and runbook links
Node, user, or lease identifiers; alert bodies; prompts; model answers; raw logs; secrets; hidden reasoning; mutations
Skill ID, version, audience, required evidence, allowed tools/data, enablement state, and bilingual runbook route
Tool credentials, unrestricted controller routes, private source paths, or an execution channel

blocks.label: Check coursebook health, then open authenticated admin diagnostics on macOS
blocks.code:
set -eu
: "${LUNANEXA_COURSEBOOK_ORIGIN:?set the approved coursebook origin}"

curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error \
  "$LUNANEXA_COURSEBOOK_ORIGIN/health"
open "$LUNANEXA_COURSEBOOK_ORIGIN/admin.html"

blocks.title: Do not manufacture administrator headers
blocks.text: Open administrator diagnostics only through the trusted signed identity proxy. If that proxy, the internal HTTPS diagnostics gateway, or its secret references are missing, keep admin diagnostics disabled; the public coursebook and read-only guide remain usable.
External prerequisites to finish before production

rows: Approved email, SMS, or webhook workers, secret references, retry policy, and dead-letter ownership
Use the durable in-app inbox and alert center; do not claim external delivery
Prometheus-compatible collector, OpenTelemetry/log collector, protected retention, dashboards, and paging integration
Local metrics, bounded events, audit, and operator alerts still work; external history and paging do not

Approved bilingual legal templates, object storage, short-lived upload exchange, malware/active-content scanner, deterministic DOCX/PDF renderer, XLSX formula/render checks, callback identity, and legal/finance policy owners
Demonstrate the workflow only; do not claim execution, settlement, invoicing, or entitlement readiness
Production IdP, trusted ingress, credential broker or SSH CA, DNS/host alias, protected provisioner and watchdog, session revocation, and tested sanitization/quarantine
Do not expose customer login or machine access
Trusted identity proxy, matching HMAC key, internal HTTPS read-only diagnostics gateway, secret-backed controller authority, network policy, and freshness monitor
Keep administrator diagnostics off; public documentation remains available

blocks.question: What should you correlate before resolving an operator alert?
blocks.answer: Confirm the typed condition has recovered, then correlate the alert's source or correlation receipt with the bounded operational event, relevant metric, and immutable audit record. Customer read state or a successful delivery alone is not recovery evidence.

pages.title: Observe, back up, and recover
pages.summary: Operate LunaNexa through bounded metrics, audit events, benchmark evidence, durable snapshots, and a fenced recovery plan. Recovery begins read-only and advances authority only after state and external effects agree.

blocks.text: Observe before changing

items: Controller /health and /version through the trusted management boundary.
Management-only /metrics with the dedicated monitoring credential.
Node heartbeat freshness, ready deployment IDs, accelerator health, queue depth, and bounded telemetry.
Deployment operation findings, assignment generations, runtime identity and health, and immutable audit receipts.
Workspace admission ownership, held concurrency, rolling-hour counters, and lease expiry.

blocks.text: Back up the complete authority set

Back up PostgreSQL plus controller registry, scheduler, assignment, enrollment, telemetry, deployment, workspace admissions, and exclusive-lease state together. Back up /data/models and signatures independently. Encrypt backups and test restoration; a file existing is not recovery evidence.

steps.title: Fence writer
steps.text: Stop or isolate the old controller and restore data into clean infrastructure.

steps.title: Raise epoch
steps.text: Start a controller with a strictly newer LUNANEXA_CONTROLLER_EPOCH.

steps.title: Reconcile only
steps.text: Set LUNANEXA_RECONCILIATION_ONLY=1 and inspect /v1/recovery/plan.

steps.title: Compare reality
steps.text: Resolve missing assignments, expired leases, orphan runtimes, active workload receipts, and unreachable nodes.

steps.title: Accept writes
steps.text: Resume normal authority only after audit continuity and idempotency are proven.

blocks.title: Do not replay an active workload blindly
blocks.text: Reconcile durable workload receipts and the upstream serving adapter's idempotency before clearing a quota or reconstructing execution.

pages.title: Debug controller, ingress, and fencing failures
pages.summary: Start from the public symptom and preserve the trust boundary. Most controller failures fall into process health, trusted ingress/authentication, configuration/rendering, network policy, or epoch fencing.

blocks.symptom: The console cannot load and the controller health endpoint is unavailable.
likely_causes: Controller pod is not ready or crash-looping.
Rendered environment, secret reference, volume, or PostgreSQL URL is missing.
Ingress route or NetworkPolicy does not reach the controller.
The browser is bypassing the trusted ingress path.
checks: Inspect Kubernetes pod status, readiness events, and bounded controller logs.
Confirm every required placeholder was resolved and management node placement is correct.
Probe /health from an allowed management pod, then through trusted ingress.
Check PostgreSQL readiness and controller connection without printing the database URL.
resolution: Fix the specific render, storage, database, or routing dependency and let Kubernetes restart normally.
Keep direct public controller access blocked; correct ingress or policy instead of widening exposure.
escalate_when: The controller repeatedly corrupts or rejects durable state.
Recovery requires a restore or epoch change.

likely_causes: A newer controller already advanced the durable fencing epoch.
An old process, assignment, or restored snapshot is attempting to write.
checks: Inspect the current durable epoch and active controller identity.
Confirm no old controller process or pod remains reachable.
Open /v1/recovery/plan from the newer reconciliation-only controller.
resolution: Do not lower or reuse the epoch. Fence the stale writer and continue recovery from the newer durable epoch.
escalate_when: Two live controllers appear to hold authority.
The durable store and observed deployment disagree about the current epoch.

blocks.symptom: Requests return Unauthenticated through a browser or remote client.
likely_causes: The correct operator, inference, audit, or monitoring credential is missing or uses the wrong scope.
Ingress did not validate the client certificate or did not inject verified auth-TLS headers.
A remote client attempted to use X-LunaNexa-Subject, which is loopback-only.
checks: Confirm the API route's required authority without echoing the secret.
Inspect ingress authentication result and header overwrite policy.
Verify the controller sees the intended trusted network peer.
resolution: Issue or route the correct scoped credential through the trusted identity boundary. Never relax the subject-header rule for remote callers.
escalate_when: A caller can spoof identity or access another authority scope.

blocks.symptom: The administrator guide diagnostics page is unavailable, stale, or missing evidence.
likely_causes: The trusted identity proxy did not replace and freshly sign the operator headers.
The server-only skill manifest or coursebook evidence index is invalid or older than its freshness threshold.
The internal HTTPS diagnostics route, controller health, operator alert, node, lease, or reconciliation endpoint is unavailable.
A required docs-namespace HMAC or controller credential reference is absent.
checks: Open /health and inspect only the optional admin_diagnostics category boolean.
Use the correlation receipt from admin.html to find the bounded GuideAdminDiagnosticRequest audit event.
Confirm the identity proxy signs the documented method/path/actor/role/timestamp payload without printing its HMAC key.
Confirm the internal route permits only the five fixed read endpoints and that every skill names its version, required evidence, allowed data, and runbook.
resolution: Repair the identity, secret reference, HTTPS route, coursebook index, or controller dependency that is explicitly marked missing; then refresh admin.html.
Keep the feature disabled if the trusted proxy or HTTPS diagnostics gateway is not available. The public coursebook and read-only pet remain independent.
escalate_when: The public pet can see live cluster state, an administrator response contains a node/user/lease identifier, or any request exposes prompts, logs, credentials, or reasoning traces.

pages.title: Debug missing nodes, blocked placement, and runtimes
pages.summary: Separate node identity, scheduler eligibility, assignment validity, artifact materialization, OCI runtime identity, health, and routing. A node appearing in inventory does not prove a model is ready.

blocks.symptom: A DGX does not appear or becomes Unreachable.
likely_causes: Kubernetes node name, LUNANEXA_NODE_ID, and inventory node_id do not match.
Bootstrap material expired, was replayed, or persistent node credential is wrong.
Heartbeat transport, certificate, clock, generation, or replay protection rejected the update.
Node agent is stopped or cannot read protected host material.
checks: Verify Kubernetes name and GPU label.
Inspect node-agent service/pod status and bounded logs.
Check certificate expiry, clock, last accepted heartbeat, and controller audit rejection code.
Confirm unique credential files exist with correct ownership without printing their contents.
resolution: Correct identity or host material, rotate through the documented certificate/bootstrap path, and wait for a current authenticated heartbeat.
escalate_when: Credential reuse or a forged/stale heartbeat is suspected.
A leased node's watchdog or helper is not protected.

blocks.symptom: A deployment is Blocked or no node is eligible.
likely_causes: Missing license, evaluation, approval, signature, secret reference, or data-class evidence.
GPU architecture, memory, runtime, model, lease, or node state fails a hard filter.
The node is cordoned, draining, unreachable, exclusively leased, or lacks the exact ready deployment heartbeat.
checks: Read typed preflight findings and placement rationale.
Compare desired artifact/runtime digests with the approved alias and live heartbeat.
Inspect accelerator free memory, health, labels, taints, lease mode, and route-map coverage.
resolution: Supply the missing reviewed evidence or restore truthful capacity/readiness. Do not edit labels to imitate a ready runtime.
escalate_when: The same snapshot produces inconsistent placement or a hard filter is bypassed.

blocks.symptom: Invocation ends with RuntimeUnavailable or readiness never converges.
likely_causes: Artifact size, digest, or signature verification failed.
Digest-pinned image is missing, wrong architecture, substituted, lacks health check, or exits.
Strict node endpoint is absent or TLS/network policy blocks it.
The serving API does not match LunaNexa's configured adapter contract.
checks: Inspect materialization and quarantine receipts.
Verify exact OCI identity and image-defined health without exposing credentials.
Probe the runtime from the approved path and compare /health and compatibility endpoint.
Confirm the selected node appears in the strict HTTPS route document.
resolution: Fix or requalify the artifact/image/route, then publish a new reviewed template or assignment generation. Do not use mutable tags or generic fallback routing.
escalate_when: Digest identity differs across registry, assignment, cache, and runtime.
The runtime leaks internal paths or credentials in its public error.

pages.title: Debug workspace authority and PostgreSQL
pages.summary: Access failures are usually correct fail-closed outcomes: subject mapping, lifecycle state, tenant scope, lease time/capability, request ownership, rate/concurrency, or database authority does not match.

likely_causes: The asserted subject is not recognized or ingress identity mapping changed.
User is invited, suspended, or revoked rather than active.
Grant is absent, revoked, expired, or belongs to another tenant.
Lease is requested, expired, revoked, wrong capability, or outside its time window.
Authority changed between self-read and admission.
checks: Read /v1/workspace/self through the same trusted identity path.
Inspect exact user, grant, tenant, lease state, capability, starts, and expiry in the console.
Check immutable prior/next audit events for recent activation, suspension, revocation, or end.
resolution: Use the typed operator lifecycle route to correct the authoritative record. Do not forge a subject header or edit the state file manually.
escalate_when: A revoked subject can still invoke or one tenant can observe another tenant's workload.

likely_causes: The capability's held-request concurrency is in use.
The rolling one-hour request limit is exhausted.
A prior controller crash conservatively holds a reservation until its bounded deadline.
checks: Inspect active workload status and cancellation ownership.
Review the .admissions state or PostgreSQL snapshot through operator tooling—not by deleting it.
Confirm deadlines and completed/cancelled releases are reconciling.
resolution: Wait for bounded release, cancel an owned active workload, or issue a reviewed lease change. Do not clear counters by deleting durable evidence.
escalate_when: A completed workload never releases held concurrency after recovery.

blocks.symptom: The controller cannot start or mutate PostgreSQL-backed authority.
likely_causes: Database URL, TLS verification, network policy, role privilege, or schema version is wrong.
Migration was not run with owner authority.
A normalized projection constraint rejected the transaction.
checks: Probe PostgreSQL readiness from the controller network boundary.
Run the idempotent migration command with a secret reference and owner role.
Inspect schema_migrations and projection row counts after restore.
Review the bounded database error without printing the URL or password.
resolution: Correct the secret-provider value, TLS trust, network rule, role, or migration; rerun the transaction after the schema is valid.
escalate_when: Snapshot and normalized projections diverge or a failed projection commits partial state.

pages.title: Configuration map
pages.summary: Configuration is deployment-owned, explicit, and separated by authority. Credentials come from a secret provider; public manifests contain references and immutable digests, never secret values.

rows: LUNANEXA_STATE_PATH, REGISTRY_PATH, ENROLLMENT_PATH, SCHEDULER_PATH, TELEMETRY_PATH, DEPLOYMENT_PATH
Back up the full set; use absolute protected paths and epoch fencing.
Use postgres in production; URL comes from secret provider with TLS verification.
Separate scopes; never place tokens in repository, URL, logs, or browser storage.
Independent authorities; node receives only matching verifier material.
Every schedulable node has one strict HTTPS route; no implicit generic fallback.
Node pulls only assigned content; runtime receives no artifact credential.
Raise monotonically and inspect recovery plan before writes.

blocks.title: Administrator settings are authoritative
blocks.text: When the validated administrator settings document is configured, legacy admission and runtime-concurrency environment overrides are migration fallbacks, not competing sources of truth.

blocks.title: Never publish configuration values from a real cluster
blocks.text: This public coursebook names variable names and meanings only. It must not contain real hosts, private addresses, database URLs, node inventories, tokens, keys, certificates, or secret-reference resolutions.

pages.title: Public error and state reference
pages.summary: Typed codes communicate which boundary rejected work. Use the code and retryability, then follow the linked diagnostic path; do not infer internal topology from a bounded public message.

rows: Required scoped credential or verified subject is absent/invalid
Correct the trusted identity or credential path; do not retry blindly.
Authenticated authority lacks the requested scope
Use the right scoped credential or request an explicit grant.
Subject, user, grant, tenant, lease, capability, or ownership does not authorize the request
Capability's held concurrent requests are in use
Wait, cancel an owned workload, or review lease capacity.
Rolling one-hour request limit is exhausted
Wait for the window or apply a reviewed lease change.
Same active workload/idempotency scope already exists
Query the existing workload; do not launch a duplicate.
Treat as terminal for that request; reassess deadline/capacity before a new logical operation.
Selected serving adapter failed or disappeared
Inspect artifact, image, readiness, route, TLS, and adapter compatibility.
A newer durable controller fenced this writer or assignment
Fence the stale process and reconcile under the newer epoch.
Node is absent or already bound by incompatible authority
Inspect enrollment, heartbeat, lease, and current node mode.
Preflight evidence or capacity is missing
Read typed findings; supply reviewed evidence before retrying.
The authenticated owner cancelled the workload
No runtime-failure escalation unless cancellation was unexpected.

blocks.title: Public errors are intentionally bounded
blocks.text: They do not contain node addresses, filesystem paths, container IDs, provider credentials, stack traces, or internal topology. Operators use correlated audit and protected logs for deeper diagnosis.

pages.title: How this coursebook was produced
pages.summary: This separate site is a MoonBook repository-coursebook projection generated from LunaNexa's current documents, source contracts, and tests. Its evidence file records the exact inspected revision, dirty state, source digests, claim status, and known gaps.

blocks.text: Projection boundary

The repository remains authoritative. This site organizes its evidence around reader questions and renders only structured text blocks. It does not execute authored HTML, embed production state, or claim that documentation generation tested the real cluster.
Freshness

blocks.title: Current repository release
blocks.text: Source revision cb490f9e passed the complete repository release gate. Physical DGX enrollment, external adapter acceptance, production PostgreSQL, and named human approval remain separate deployment gates and are not implied by this repository release.
The read-only documentation pet

The Ask guide panel is optional. A same-origin server sends the published coursebook and public evidence projection to MoonClaw's existing read-only Cowork endpoint. The adapter validates a narrow answer schema and known page citations. It cannot edit LunaNexa, run commands, expose gateway details, or substitute for operator authority.
Lessons adapted from the Suanli reference

items: Stable product-level navigation above a grouped documentation sidebar.
One focused article with a right-side on-page outline.
Search prominent in the global header.
Clear product overview, quickstart, use instructions, FAQ/debugging, best practices, and prebuilt runtime routes.
LunaNexa adds explicit evidence status, production gaps, trust boundaries, and a source ledger rather than copying Suanli's brand or claims.

blocks.question: What should happen when LunaNexa source changes?
blocks.answer: Re-run the repository evidence scan, update source digests and claim statuses, regenerate coursebook.json, exercise the site and pet states, and review meaning before publishing.
